name: Sika Sigunit L-530 AF
paste:
SIKA® SIGUNIT® L-530 AF: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® Sigunit® L-530 AF, August 2024, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/n/sika_sigunit_l-530af.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® Sigunit® L-530 AF where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (August 2024, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. Sika® Sigunit® L-530 AF is a high-performance liquid, alkali-free, setting and hardening accelerator for shotcrete. Sika® Sigunit® L-530 AF is a solution based product and no circulation is required to keep Sika® Sigunit® L-530 AF homogenised.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sigunit®L-530 AF is suitable for both dry and wet spraying processes and it is used for:
    - Support at the face, wall & backs whilst advancing tunnels and mines
    - Rock- and slope stabilisation
    - High quality lining shotcrete
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.4.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® Sigunit® L-530 AF
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Liquid alkali-free set accelerator for shotcrete
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (August 2024, Version 01.02) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer. Sika® Sigunit® L-530 AF liquid shotcrete set accelerator has the following characteristics and advantages:
    - No circulation required
    - No waste due to settlement
    - High early strength development
    - Alkali-free
    - Minimal strength loss of the accelerated concrete
    - No pollution of groundwater by leached out alkalis
    - Distinct reduction of rebound and dust
    - Improves bond of shotcrete to rock and concrete thus facilitating overhead spraying
    - Chloride-free, does not negatively affect the reinforcement steel
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Aqueous solution of selected inorganic materials.
    - Appearance and colour: Cloudy white liquid
    - Specific gravity: 1.46 g/cm³
    - pH-Value: 3.0 approximately
    - Viscosity: ≤ 120 mPa s at +20°C
2.5 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Total chloride ion content: ≤ 0.1%
    - Equivalent sodium oxide: ≤ 1.0%
    - Restrictions: If thicker layers of shotcrete are to be applied, ensure that the temperature of the basic concrete is not lower than +15°C. Lower temperatures require higher dosage of accelerator.
2.6 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 1000 litre IBC
    - Shelf life: Eight (8) months from date of production if stored in original, unopened, undamaged and sealed containers, protected from direct sunlight and kept at temperatures between +5°C and +35°C.
    - Storage conditions: Store at temperature between 5°C and 35°C protected from direct sunlight. After prolonged storage the performance of Sika® Sigunit® L-530 AF should be tested.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (August 2024, Version 01.02) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (August 2024, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Recommended dosage: For layer thicknesses of up to 100 mm in one pass, dosage is between 4% and 7% of weight of binder. The correct dosage must be determined by preliminary testing.
4.3 Compatibility. The following Sika® products are generally used for the basic shotcrete mix: Sika® ViscoCrete® product range; SikaTard®-960 HC; SikaMix®; Sika® Stabilizer 4R AU and Sika® Stabilizer-821 CS; Sigunit®L-530 AF is not compatible with alkaline shotcrete accelerators.
4.4 Limitations and important considerations.
    - The substrate must be clean, free of loose stones and free of water under hydrostatic pressure.
    - The accelerator’s effect depends on the cement content, the age and type of cement, on the substrate and the shotcrete temperature as well as on the layer thickness and spraying process, quality of equipment and application technique. The w/c ratio of the basic concrete mix in the wet spraying process, and the quantity of gauging water in the dry spraying process are also parameters influencing the acceleration effect of Sigunit®L-530 AF.
    - Before using Sigunit®L-530 AF the accelerator hoses must be cleaned thoroughly. The use of Sigunit®L-530 AF requires technically correct dosing and conveying / spraying technology. Metal parts of the pump that come into direct contact with Sigunit®L-530 AF must be made of stainless steel
4.5 Further documentation. When using sulphate resistant cements strength development can be slower.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.4):
    - The accelerator’s effect depends on the cement content, the age and type of cement, on the substrate and the shotcrete temperature as well as on the layer thickness and spraying process, quality of equipment and application technique. The w/c ratio of the basic concrete mix in the wet spraying process, and the quantity of gauging water in the dry spraying process are also parameters influencing the acceleration effect of Sigunit®L-530 AF.
5.3 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.4 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® Sigunit® L-530 AF, August 2024, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/n/sika_sigunit_l-530af.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sika® Sigunit® L-530 AF, version 18/06/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/w/sds-sika-sigunitl-530af.pdf
    - Environmental Product Declaration: Sika® Sigunit® L-530 AF EPD, version 03/09/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/8/sika-sigunit-l-530afepd.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
